blocks.text: Homeostasis is maintained by three elements working together.

items: Receptors (sensors): organs, tissues, cells or parts of cells that detect changes and send the information to the control centre, for example temperature receptors in the skin and pressure receptors in blood vessels.

Control centre: receives the information, processes it and sends messages to the effectors so the internal environment stays within a narrow range around set points; the brain, spinal cord and endocrine glands act as control centres.

Effectors: muscles and glands that respond, muscles by contracting and glands by secreting, restoring the set point. When body temperature drops, shivering and vasoconstriction raise heat production and reduce heat loss.

blocks.alt: A clockwise cycle. A change in the internal environmental condition tips an 'Imbalance' plank on a see-saw labelled 'Internal conditions (in homeostasis)'. The change is detected by the receptor, information is sent to the control centre, a message is sent to the effector, and the response of the effector returns the condition to normal.
blocks.caption: Figure 13.1: Elements of homeostasis (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 13.1).
blocks.long_description: Receptor (blue box, left), control centre (pink, top) and effector (green, right) sit on the cycle. The arrows are labelled 'Change detected by receptor', 'Information sent to control centre', 'Message sent to Effector' and 'Response of effector to return the condition to normal'. At the bottom a see-saw carries the level plank 'Internal conditions (in homeostasis)' and a tilted plank marked 'Imbalance' at both ends; a small arrow under the raised end is labelled 'Change in internal environmental condition'.
